summary: Python 2 mixes bytes and text loosely until non-ASCII input breaks things, while Python 3 strictly separates them, so Ansible chooses a string strategy per code area.
questions: Why do non-ASCII strings break Python 2 code?
How do bytes and text differ in Python 3?

answer_card.title: Bytes vs text in Python 2 and 3
answer_card.answer_md: Python 2's `str` (bytes) and `unicode` (text) mix freely for ASCII but throw errors with non-ASCII. Python 3 strictly separates `bytes` and `str` and errors on mixing, forcing an explicit strategy. Ansible uses different strategies for control node code, modules and module_utils.
